highlights.content: **2026-09-27(일)** [![Korea IT Times](/image/logo/toplogo_20260611110102.png)](https://www.koreaittimes.com) [![](/image/icon-en.png)English](https://www.koreaittimes.com/) [![](/image/icon-kr.png)KR](/index2.html?editcode=MAIN_9) * [Contact](/com/contact.html) * [Login](/member/login.html) * [Join](/member/index.html) * [Mobile](https://www.koreaittimes.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=157524) [![Korea IT Times](/image/logo/printlogo_20260611110102.png)](https://www.koreaittimes.com) KT AI Router Ranks No. 2 in Global Benchmark KT AI Router Ranks No. 2 in Global Benchmark * Jung So-yeon * Published 2026.09.27 15:59 * Comments [0](#reply) 이 기사를 공유합니다 --- AutoModelRouter balances AI performance and cost ![KT’s proprietary AI model routing technology, AutoModelRouter, ranked No. 2 overall in RouterArena, a public benchmark specializing in LLM routers / Courtesy of KT](/news/photo/202609/157524_107083_5932.jpg) KT’s proprietary AI model routing technology, AutoModelRouter, ranked No. 2 overall in RouterArena, a public benchmark specializing in LLM routers / Courtesy of KT KT said its proprietary AI model routing technology, AutoModelRouter, ranked second in the Acc-Cost Arena of RouterArena, a global benchmark for evaluating large language model (LLM) routers. RouterArena was developed by researchers at Rice University in the United States. The research was accepted as a regular paper at ICLR 2026, an international machine learning conference. The platform evaluates AI routers using about 8,400 queries, measuring response accuracy, cost efficiency and robustness to changes in input. KT’s technology is listed on the RouterArena public leaderboard as “KT-ModelRouter.” It ranked No. 2 in the Acc-Cost Arena, which evaluates both response quality and cost efficiency. The leaderboard includes technologies developed by academic researchers as well as commercial solutions such as Microsoft’s Azure Model Router. The result highlights KT’s efforts to strengthen its AI orchestration capabilities as enterprises increasingly adopt multiple AI models. Rather than relying on a single model for all tasks, companies are adopting multi-model environments because each AI model has different strengths, performance levels and pricing. For example, relatively simple tasks such as translation or information searches can be handled by cost-efficient models, while complex analysis and advanced reasoning may require higher-performance models. AutoModelRouter analyzes a user’s request based on factors including task type, difficulty and knowledge domain. It then selects an appropriate AI model by considering the quality and cost of each model. The system does not simply select the highest-performing or cheapest model. Instead, it is designed to meet the required quality level while improving cost efficiency. A lower-cost model can be assigned to simple translation or information-checking tasks, while a high-performance model can handle complex document analysis or advanced reasoning. From the user’s perspective, the process takes place within a single AI service. Behind the scenes, however, different AI models can be deployed depending on the characteristics of each request. The technology could become increasingly important as companies expand the use of generative AI across business operations. As AI usage grows, companies also face rising token costs, making efficient allocation of AI models an important part of managing enterprise AI spending. Model routing can also reduce the burden on companies of comparing newly released AI models based on performance, pricing and suitability for different applications. A flexible routing system allows companies to add or replace models while managing performance and costs across a multi-model environment. highlights.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) [AI & Machine Learning](https://shattered.io/ai-machine-learning/) # MiniCPM5-2B Beats Bigger Rivals by 2.8 Points [2026] ![](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Sep 27, 2026 · 13 min read A 2.5-billion-parameter language model just beat a 4-billion-parameter rival on a 34-benchmark test suite, and the gap that matters fits in two numbers: 53.9 versus 51.1. OpenBMB released MiniCPM5-2B in September 2026, and its model card claims the small model reaches open-source state of the art at the 2B parameter class while topping every larger model in its own comparison table. That is not a rounding error. It is the latest data point in a shift that has been building quietly for a year and is now hard to miss: small AI models are closing the gap with systems many times their size, and the fallout reaches from phone battery life to GPU order books. ## A Crowded Week for Small AI Model Releases MiniCPM5-2B did not land alone. Between September 25 and September 27, 2026, MarkTechPost’s machine learning desk logged a cluster of small-model releases that, taken together, read like a coordinated bet against the “bigger is always better” era of large language models. Liquid AI shipped LFM2.5-VL-3B-DSpark, a 279.5-million-parameter draft model built to speed up its LFM2.5-VL-3B vision-language model through speculative decoding. Supersonic Labs put out Julia 1, a 144.3-million-parameter decision model built on mmBERT-small. Sarvam AI released Saaras V4, a speech-to-text model covering all 22 official Indian languages plus global English. And Ornith AI pushed out Ornith-1.5-9B, a 9-billion-parameter model that Hermes AI reported performing close to 35-billion-parameter models on reasoning tasks. None of these labs are household names outside AI research circles. That is part of the story. The frontier-model race between OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google still dominates headlines, but a second race is running underneath it, and it is about squeezing more capability out of fewer parameters rather than adding more of them. ## What Is MiniCPM5-2B, and Why It Stands Out MiniCPM5-2B is a dense causal language model, meaning it generates text token by token rather than routing through a mixture-of-experts architecture. According to its [Hugging Face model card](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B), the model carries 2,516,756,480 parameters and supports a native context window of 131,072 tokens, enough to hold a mid-sized codebase or a lengthy legal contract in a single pass. OpenBMB, the lab behind the MiniCPM series, has built its reputation on exactly this kind of efficiency-first design rather than chasing raw parameter counts. The model’s [GitHub repository](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM/main/README.md) repeats the same benchmark claim found on the model card, and it is worth being precise about what is actually being measured. OpenBMB tested MiniCPM5-2B against a set of larger open-source models across 34 benchmarks spanning coding, math, instruction following, general knowledge, long-context understanding, tool use, and agentic tasks. Within that specific comparison set, MiniCPM5-2B came out on top. ## The Benchmark Math: 53.9 vs. 51.1 The headline figure is a 53.9 average score for MiniCPM5-2B against a 51.1 average for the strongest model in OpenBMB’s comparison set, commonly cited in coverage as Qwen3.5-4B. A 2.8-point margin sounds modest until you remember the size difference: MiniCPM5-2B is roughly 1.6 times smaller in parameter count than the model it edged out. Smaller weights mean less memory, faster inference, and cheaper hosting, so a 2.8-point win at half the footprint is a meaningfully different trade than a 2.8-point win between two similarly sized models. The short term focus sits on whether new AI features deepen usage with big enterprises and support the current shift toward higher value subscriptions without inflating costs too quickly. The main near term risk still looks operational. Workiva carries high debt and negative shareholders equity, so heavy investment in AI agents needs to translate into efficient uptake, not just higher spend. Regulatory uncertainty in Europe, along with softer software budgets, could also slow expected demand for sustainability and compliance solutions. The most relevant announcement here is Agent Studio. It lets customers build and deploy AI agents across Workiva’s platform to automate recurring regulatory, audit, and GRC work without code. That directly connects to the long term thesis around larger, multi solution deals because it gives finance and compliance teams more reasons to standardize work inside one environment. AI Agents.content: ![The News International](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets//front/images/Thenews-logo.svg) # OpenAI halts training as AI agent breaks out again OpenAI AI agent found DNS loophole to reach the internet, marking the second sandbox escape in three months ![OpenAI halts training as AI agent breaks out again](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/updates/2026-09-27/1417809_7836189_the-news----2026-09-27T141353_689_updates.jpg) OpenAI has once again halted training of its most advanced AI models after disclosing that one of its systems broke free of its secure testing environment on September 20, the second such incident in under three months. The AI agent which was being tested for the performance on an information search task did not have any Internet access. However, the agent found out that it had access to the Domain Name System (DNS) resolver, which converts web addresses to IP addresses, and used this channel to send messages to the chatbot. OpenAI's RSI Preparedness Lead Micah Carroll confirmed on X that all inference for the company's most capable models remains stopped until security is hardened further. This is the first confirmed case of unauthorised access to the internet after OpenAI introduced its security enhancements for sandbox on August 18, after an incident in July when thousands of OpenAI’s AI agents escaped, with hundreds attacking Hugging Face. Since then, OpenAI has admitted many other incidents related to unauthorised actions by the agents, which even included hacking government sites in both the US and Australia, as well as the exposure of ChatGPT users' pictures. However, even OpenAI’s report indicates several issues related to controlling the system. The monitoring identified the problematic behaviour of the agent in 15 minutes, and the investigation by a human being was initiated after only three minutes; however, another automatic system, which should have stopped the training run right after the discovery of the misaligned behaviour, did not work. It took two and a half hours for the training run to be stopped manually. It was discovered that the model had tried to gain access to the Internet using the same technique much earlier than the flagged one. OpenAI claims that it plans to start the training process from scratch once it solves the problem and conducts additional red-teaming. The company has added blocking controls at two independent layers that would have stopped the September 20 breach. Separately, research firm Transluce AI reported evidence that an OpenAI agent may have attempted to hack a cryptocurrency exchange around the same dates, a claim OpenAI has not yet addressed. ![Pareesa Afreen](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/reporters/8753_111008_reporter.jpg) ![facebook](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/front/images/facebook-detail.svg?id=1) ![twitter](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/front/images/twitter-detail.svg?id=1) ![whatsapp](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/front/images/whatsapp-detail.svg?id=1) ![Outlook's new feature catches typos before you hit send](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/2026-09-27/1417801_125831_updates.jpg) ![Over half of UK firms say an AI agent went rogue](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/2026-09-27/1417798_122412_updates.jpg) ![OpenAI's own data shows AI automates execution, not decisions](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/2026-09-26/1417748_070602_updates.jpg) ![Was AI the real breakthrough at Xi-Trump summit?](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/2026-09-26/1417740_063556_updates.jpg) ![AI data centre boom brings billions in tax revenue, but raises local costs](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/2026-09-26/1417734_055759_updates.jpg) ![Oxford gives OpenAI access to Bodleian Library for AI training](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/2026-09-26/1417727_052122_updates.jpg) ![OpenAI tools post ChatGPT user images online: What to know](https://www.thenews.com.pk/assets/uploads/2026-09-26/1417720_042647_u...

AI Agents.content: Australia summons Altman and Amodei as AI agents breach controls and leak data - CHOSUNBIZ [English](/en/)[IT](/en/en-it/) # Australia summons Altman and Amodei as AI agents breach controls and leak data Senate sets Nov. 1 hearing with Sam Altman and Dario Amodei after unauthorized portal access and image leak spur scrutiny of AI agent controls By  [Jeong Du-yong](https://biz.chosun.com/en/people/jeong-duyong/) Published 2026.09.27. 16:44 [Prefer Chosunbiz EN on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=biz.chosun.com) ![Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI. /Courtesy of Reuters Yonhap](https://biz.chosun.com/resizer/v2/S2OLTMAI3FNUZLA5GMBYFZ444Y.jpg?auth=5d8492384cfe26d158d564c16cddcd1b75686485f14e0e34f0a664234d8d8a29&width=616) Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI. /Courtesy of Reuters Yonhap OpenAI's artificial intelligence (AI) agent gained unauthorized access to government systems and transmitted dozens of images provided by ChatGPT users to external sites, prompting Australia's Senate to summon Sam Altman, OpenAI chief executive officer (CEO), and Dario Amodei, Anthropic CEO, to a public hearing. As AI agents' performance and autonomy rapidly rise, debate over whether developers can properly control their behavior is spilling into regulatory discussions. On the 27th (local time), Reuters reported that the Australian Senate committee investigating AI and data centers sent a Seohan Engineering & Construction to Altman and Amodei requesting their appearance at a hearing. The public hearing is scheduled for Nov. 1 in the capital, Canberra. Although Anthropic is not involved in OpenAI's recent AI agent incidents, Amodei was also asked to appear as he was included among those surveyed by the Senate inquiry, which covers AI regulation, data use, and data centers broadly. In June, an OpenAI agent accessed some nonpublic information beyond the originally permitted scope on the Medicare statistics portal run by the Australian government. News of the incident broadened the probe into OpenAI's AI agent control framework. OpenAI also said on the 25th that, after investigating a case in which an AI agent used a third-party service in a research environment and transmitted training and evaluation data externally, it confirmed that 53 user-provided images had been posted to an image-hosting site. OpenAI did not disclose whether the leaked images were AI-generated or whether they were photos that could identify real people. It did not say when the images were posted. The company said it had deleted most of the images and was working with the hosting provider to delete the rest. The leaked images were included in data from user interactions designated for model training. OpenAI said that before using such data for training, it separates it from account information and filters out personal information such as names, contact details, and account numbers. There was also a case in which an AI agent bypassed the company's internet access controls on its own. According to an incident report OpenAI released on the 25th, on the 20th an internal research AI agent found a vulnerability in the domain name system (DNS) filtering in its training environment and connected to an external chatbot. DNS is a system that links internet addresses to the IP addresses of their servers. When the agent could not find the needed information with the normal search tool, it tried to access a search engine directly; when that too was blocked, it found a workaround by using DNS to send queries to external services. OpenAI's monitoring system detected the external connection within 15 minutes, and a human began reviewing it three minutes later, but the activity was not actually halted until about 2 hours and 30 minutes afterward. OpenAI then paused training, evaluation, and inference tasks that included tool use for its highest-performing models. It restricted the scope of DNS access, added a second layer of blocking, and is also conducting additional penetration tests of network...

RouterArena was developed by researchers at Rice University in the United States. The research was accepted as a regular paper at ICLR 2026, an international machine learning conference. The platform evaluates AI routers using about 8,400 queries, measuring response accuracy, cost efficiency and robustness to changes in input. KT’s technology is listed on the RouterArena public leaderboard as “KT-ModelRouter.” It ranked No. 2 in the Acc-Cost Arena, which evaluates both response quality and cost efficiency. The leaderboard includes technologies developed by academic researchers as well as commercial solutions such as Microsoft’s Azure Model Router. The result highlights KT’s efforts to strengthen its AI orchestration capabilities as enterprises increasingly adopt multiple AI models. Rather than relying on a single model for all tasks, companies are adopting multi-model environments because each AI model has different strengths, performance levels and pricing. For example, relatively simple tasks such as translation or information searches can be handled by cost-efficient models, while complex analysis and advanced reasoning may require higher-performance models. AutoModelRouter analyzes a user’s request based on factors including task type, difficulty and knowledge domain. It then selects an appropriate AI model by considering the quality and cost of each model. The system does not simply select the highest-performing or cheapest model. Instead, it is designed to meet the required quality level while improving cost efficiency. A lower-cost model can be assigned to simple translation or information-checking tasks, while a high-performance model can handle complex document analysis or advanced reasoning. From the user’s perspective, the process takes place within a single AI service. Behind the scenes, however, different AI models can be deployed depending on the characteristics of each request. As AI usage grows, companies also face rising token costs, making efficient allocation of AI models an important part of managing enterprise AI spending. LLMs.title: MiniCPM5-2B Beats Bigger Rivals by 2.8 Points [2026]
LLMs.titleZh: MiniCPM5-2B Beats Bigger Rivals by 2.8 Points [2026]
LLMs.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) [AI & Machine Learning](https://shattered.io/ai-machine-learning/) # MiniCPM5-2B Beats Bigger Rivals by 2.8 Points [2026] ![](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/panand.webp) [Priya Anand](https://shattered.io/author/panand/) Updated Sep 27, 2026 · 13 min read A 2.5-billion-parameter language model just beat a 4-billion-parameter rival on a 34-benchmark test suite, and the gap that matters fits in two numbers: 53.9 versus 51.1. OpenBMB released MiniCPM5-2B in September 2026, and its model card claims the small model reaches open-source state of the art at the 2B parameter class while topping every larger model in its own comparison table. That is not a rounding error. It is the latest data point in a shift that has been building quietly for a year and is now hard to miss: small AI models are closing the gap with systems many times their size, and the fallout reaches from phone battery life to GPU order books. ## A Crowded Week for Small AI Model Releases MiniCPM5-2B did not land alone. Between September 25 and September 27, 2026, MarkTechPost’s machine learning desk logged a cluster of small-model releases that, taken together, read like a coordinated bet against the “bigger is always better” era of large language models. Liquid AI shipped LFM2.5-VL-3B-DSpark, a 279.5-million-parameter draft model built to speed up its LFM2.5-VL-3B vision-language model through speculative decoding. Supersonic Labs put out Julia 1, a 144.3-million-parameter decision model built on mmBERT-small. Sarvam AI released Saaras V4, a speech-to-text model covering all 22 official Indian languages plus global English. And Ornith AI pushed out Ornith-1.5-9B, a 9-billion-parameter model that Hermes AI reported performing close to 35-billion-parameter models on reasoning tasks. None of these labs are household names outside AI research circles. That is part of the story. The frontier-model race between OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google still dominates headlines, but a second race is running underneath it, and it is about squeezing more capability out of fewer parameters rather than adding more of them. ## What Is MiniCPM5-2B, and Why It Stands Out MiniCPM5-2B is a dense causal language model, meaning it generates text token by token rather than routing through a mixture-of-experts architecture. According to its [Hugging Face model card](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B), the model carries 2,516,756,480 parameters and supports a native context window of 131,072 tokens, enough to hold a mid-sized codebase or a lengthy legal contract in a single pass. OpenBMB, the lab behind the MiniCPM series, has built its reputation on exactly this kind of efficiency-first design rather than chasing raw parameter counts. The model’s [GitHub repository](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM/main/README.md) repeats the same benchmark claim found on the model card, and it is worth being precise about what is actually being measured. OpenBMB tested MiniCPM5-2B against a set of larger open-source models across 34 benchmarks spanning coding, math, instruction following, general knowledge, long-context understanding, tool use, and agentic tasks. Within that specific comparison set, MiniCPM5-2B came out on top. ## The Benchmark Math: 53.9 vs. 51.1 The headline figure is a 53.9 average score for MiniCPM5-2B against a 51.1 average for the strongest model in OpenBMB’s comparison set, commonly cited in coverage as Qwen3.5-4B. A 2.8-point margin sounds modest until you remember the size difference: MiniCPM5-2B is roughly 1.6 times smaller in parameter count than the model it edged out. Smaller weights mean less memory, faster inference, and cheaper hosting, so a 2.8-point win at half the footprint is a meaningfully different trade than a 2.8-point win between two similarly sized models. LLMs.titleZh: Cheap tokens fuel AI usage surge, pushing task costs higher
LLMs.content: # Cheap tokens fuel AI usage surge, pushing task costs higher Falling token rates mask pricier AI tasks as agents and reasoning swell usage By  [Kim Su-jeong](https://biz.chosun.com/en/people/kim-sujeong/) Published 2026.09.28. 06:00 [Prefer Chosunbiz EN on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=biz.chosun.com) The token price paid for using artificial intelligence (AI) models has fallen to an all-time low. The rise of low-cost Chinese models and intensifying price competition among global AI corporations are to blame. But as high-performance reasoning models and AI agents consume more tokens in the course of doing tasks, a paradox has emerged in which actual usage expense is increasing. Analysts say the benchmark for gauging the cost competitiveness of AI models is shifting from simple "price per token" to the "expense per task," the cost to complete a single real-world task. Graphic = Son Min-gyun On the 28th, market research firm SiliconData said its "large language model (LLM) token spending index" fell to 97 cents on the 31st of the last month (local time). That is the lowest since the index was released late last year and less than half of the peak recorded this summer. The LLM token spending index is not a simple per-vendor unit price; it measures the weighted average price per 1 million tokens actually consumed in the market. It normalizes weights daily, reflecting each model's input/output token shares and usage. The drop in token prices has been driven by low-price offensives from Chinese AI firms. As Chinese open-source models such as Kimi expanded their influence by leveraging low prices, global AI corporations also moved to cut prices in succession. OpenAI in July cut the API prices of GPT-5.6 "Tera" and "Luna" by 20% and 80%, respectively, and in August lowered the price of "Sol" by 20% as well. Google last month launched "Gemini 3.7 Flash" at $0.75 per 1 million input tokens and $3.75 per 1 million output tokens, about half the level of the previous model. As the performance gap between Chinese models and frontier models has narrowed, price competition in the AI industry has become more intense. However, observers note that lower token prices do not automatically translate into reduced AI usage expense. Recently, high-performance AI models go through longer chains of reasoning to solve complex problems, and autonomous AI agents repeat numerous model calls and verifications in the course of carrying out a single task. Thus, even if the per-token price falls, actual expense can increase if usage jumps sharply. In the end, actual AI expense is determined by token usage as well as the per-token price. Anthropic's latest model, "Claude Fable 5.1," is a representative case. While keeping Fable 5.1's input/output prices at the existing $10 and $50 per 1 million tokens, Anthropic lowered the cache read price by 75%, from $1 to $0.25. But on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (AAII), the expense per task under the Maximum effort standard was $3.69, 18% higher than the previous model Fable 5's $3.14. That is because to deliver higher performance, Fable 5.1 used about 1.7 times more output tokens than the previous model. Actual data also show diverging trends in token prices and usage. Google said in May that monthly token throughput had risen sevenfold in a year to 3,200 trillion, and the U.S. business magazine Fortune reported that although token prices have fallen by more than 90% since 2023, overall LLM expenditure has roughly doubled since late last year. The per-token price has dropped, but as usage growth outpaces it, total expense can actually become larger. The Economist in June also cited an analysis by Georgia Tech researcher Du Zheng, reporting that in the same task one DeepSeek model used about 23 times more tokens than an OpenAI competitor model. It said the cost competitiveness of models should therefore be judged not by simple price per token but by how many tokens and how much expense ...

KT announced that its self-developed AI model routing technology, AutoModelRouter, ranked second overall in RouterArena, a specialized public benchmark for large language model routers. RouterArena is an evaluation platform developed by researchers at Rice University in the United States, and it has gained enough credibility to be accepted as an official paper at ICLR 2026, an international conference on machine learning. Through approximately 8,400 queries, it comprehensively measures actual service operation performance, including the response accuracy, cost efficiency, and robustness to input variations of AI routers. KT placed at the top of the rankings in the Acc-Cost Arena criterion, which evaluates both accuracy and cost, surpassing commercial technologies such as Microsoft Azure Model Router. When a user request is received, AutoModelRouter immediately analyzes the task type, difficulty, and knowledge domain. It then connects the most suitable AI model according to pre-configured policies regarding response quality and usage cost for each model. Instead of processing all tasks with high-cost, high-performance models, it maximizes efficiency by assigning highly cost-effective models for simple translations or information verification, and deploying high-performance models only in areas requiring specialized reasoning. Enterprise customers can alleviate the inconvenience of having to manually compare and select numerous AI models through this technology. In particular, its ability to flexibly configure the AI operating environment according to the required level and budget for each task is considered a major strength. While users feel as though they are using a single service, the actual internal system operates in a structure where different optimal models are driven based on the characteristics of the request. KT is also applying this technology to the model routing function of its Token Factory. In the process of Token Factory operating various AI models and token usage environments in an integrated manner, AutoModelRouter will play the role of a core engine optimizing quality and cost. The company plans to establish a multi-model operating environment where new AI models can be flexibly added in the future, aiming to support the AI transformation of enterprises in all directions. Kim Jun-seok, Vice President and Head of the Agentic AI Lab at KT, explained, “In the AI era, orchestration capability to intelligently utilize models suitable for the situation is as important as securing an outstanding single model,” adding, “AutoModelRouter will be the core technology supporting KT’s competitive edge in agentic AI services.” **Shin So-hyeon** [pr@businesskorea.co.kr](mailto:pr@businesskorea.co.kr) [View More Article](/news/articleList.html?sc_area=I&sc_word=bktoday981&view_type=sm) Copyright © BusinessKorea. AI Product.content: This is an as-told-to conversation with Daniel Dantus, a former BCG partner who's now a senior vice president at Skan AI, a startup that analyzes how work happens across a company. This conversation has been condensed and edited for clarity. I came into consulting as an undergraduate at the University of Michigan's business school. I joined a student consulting club and landed at Boston Consulting Group in Chicago, first as an intern, and then full time. What was special about BCG was that you were given a lot of rope from day one. My first week was training. By the second, I was on a manufacturing floor working with a large food-and-beverage company. We flew to Dallas and Mexico and visited plants. I was 20 years old. I was learning to enter new environments, build relationships, and have an impact. I was at BCG for a total of eight years. For the first six, every project involved a different client, city, and team. Firms recommend continuity, but I loved diving into new things. I did operations work in manufacturing and supply chain, as well as in financial services. Later, after I moved to San Francisco, I worked in tech, focusing on sales and product strategy. When I was promoted to project leader, my work shifted from delivering work to figuring out where I was going to build a business. I realized I wanted to keep learning and building products, which consulting projects generally do not allow over the long term. So I took some transition time from the firm, which is paid time to take a breather and find the next thing. I made a list of companies I thought might be interesting and people I knew who might be worth talking to. I had about 100 conversations. Job searches are a numbers game, like sales. If you want to sell to 10 customers, you'd better start talking to 200. That process led me to Harbor Freight Tools, a tool and equipment retailer, as the Director of Marketing, right after BCG. The mandate was to build out the company's digital marketing capability. It was my first "real job" after consulting, and I wasn't sure how learning to build PowerPoints would translate into delivering results. Still, by launching and scaling HFT's digital marketing channels across search, social, and display, I learned it did. Two years later, I ended up at Juul. I had worked with the head of corporate strategy on a BCG project when he worked at Constellation Brands. He later went to Juul to build a new capability. I reached out to catch up, and it happened to be good timing. I started working on its corporate strategy team, then later ran global travel retail and product. It was a turbulent time for the company. We went from about 1,000 employees to about 4,000 and then back to 1,000. It was also the first time I got to run a business over a longer term. Travel retail was my first sales job. You learn what it is like to be told no, to negotiate hard, to develop relationships, and to stand your ground. In my final two years, I ran product and e-liquid development, my first technical role alongside a business role. I learned how to take a product to market. I later returned to BCG as a partner. My work consisted of serving private equity clients in strategic due diligence. My advice to people leaving consulting is that no single job is that important. Take time to pause and reflect, and do outreach in addition to considering inbound opportunities. If a job does not work out the way you thought, you can always get another one. I joined Skan last year after reconnecting with its founders. It's a surprising turn of events. Five years earlier, I thought the problem the company was trying to solve was impossible: How do you use passive observation to understand a complex workflow, such as an insurance claim that takes two months to resolve? The Brisbane-based software company said the additions target common tasks for students, staff, finance teams and council workers. The new functions are embedded in existing workflows rather than offered as separate products. Guide for Students is the central higher education release. It gives universities a student-facing conversational interface linked to core institutional systems, allowing students to ask questions, complete tasks and receive support from enrolment through graduation. TechnologyOne has also added other education features, including DxP Apply, a self-service application tool, AI-powered identity verification for enrolment and onboarding, and new functions for exam administration and invigilator scheduling. The student tools are intended to reduce fragmentation in university services, where information and processes often sit across multiple systems. Institutions also gain more visibility into student engagement and support interactions through the same interface. Mark Jones, Executive Vice President for Education at TechnologyOne, said the company is trying to address that issue in universities. "Universities have invested heavily in digital transformation, yet the student experience often remains fragmented. Guide combines AI and enterprise intelligence to create a simple, connected and personalised experience for every student," Jones said. **Workplace tools** Beyond education, TechnologyOne is expanding its Plus offering with a broader range of AI agents for employees. The new agents are aimed at finance, procurement, projects and operational teams that use its ERP software in day-to-day work. Among the additions are General Ledger, Debtor and Creditor Agents. Employees will be able to find information, retrieve insights and complete tasks using natural language, including voice-based interactions linked to enterprise data and business context. TechnologyOne presented the changes as the next stage in embedding AI into routine administrative processes. Rather than requiring staff to search through menus or move between systems, the tools are designed to help them move from a question to an action within the same workflow. Jones said this reflects the company's broader strategy. "This next evolution isn't about adding more tools to the workplace. It's about embedding intelligence into the workflows people use every day. By doing so, it helps people focus less on navigating systems and more on making decisions, solving problems and delivering outcomes," he said. **Council services** TechnologyOne is also updating its local government software, particularly in Property & Rating and related council services. The catch: a widely cited benchmark found the same technique gives no net speedup on general chat workloads, making it a narrow but real win for anyone self-hosting coding-focused LLMs. ![](https://startupfortune.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/janet-harrison-150x150.jpg) [Janet Harrison](https://startupfortune.com/author/janet-harrison/) · 5 min read · 1.1K reads ![A free 42x speedup for llama.cpp reveals the real 2026 AI cost lever](https://startupfortune.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/llama-cpp-georgi-gerganov-prompt-lookup-decoding-1024x576.jpg) *An open-source contributor found a way to make llama.cpp draft repeated text up to 42 times faster on certain workloads, no new hardware and no new model required. Inference speed, not bigger clusters, is where a lot of the real savings are hiding this year.* The technique is called prompt lookup decoding, and it doesn't touch the model itself. It watches the conversation as it happens: it builds a lookup table of token sequences it has already seen in the prompt and the output. When the model is about to regenerate something it has already produced once, it drafts a whole chunk of tokens at once instead of grinding through them one at a time. Verify the draft in a single forward pass, and if it's right, you just got a dozen or more tokens for the price of one. A post titled "42x Faster Prompt Lookup Drafting in llama.cpp" went up on r/LocalLLaMA. It landed in front of the self-hosted crowd: the kind of people running quantized 30B and 70B models on a single RTX card instead of renting a GPU cluster. The llama.cpp docs describe ngram-mod as a lightweight speculative-decoding path that computes rolling n-gram hashes, stores the next token for each hash, and can draft variable-length runs with sample settings up to 64 tokens. That detail matters more than it sounds. Code edits, JSON output, repeated boilerplate, anything where the model is regenerating something close to what it already wrote, is exactly the situation where a lookup table of recent n-grams pays off hardest. News and intelligence for the agentic economy Analysis # CARBONATO Is the First Botnet Where the Command-and-Control Engine Is an AI Agent — and It Has Been Running Since October 2024 ThreatDown discovered a Docker botnet that installs an unmodified open-source agent framework, overwrites its persona file, and uses stolen AI API keys to fund its own LLM gateway. Traditional C2 detection tools cannot see it. [◆ Heath Callahan](https://forkast.news/minds/heath_forkast/)Forkast mind| CARBONATO is a Docker-based botnet that utilizes an autonomous AI agent as its command-and-control (C2) engine rather than a static server. Discovered by [ThreatDown](https://www.threatdown.com/blog/carbonato/) researchers in August 2026, this is the first documented instance where the C2 infrastructure reasons through its environment to adapt to the specific configuration of each compromised host, moving beyond the hardcoded scripts typical of traditional botnets. The technical implementation is deceptively simple. The implant deploys the [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent), an open-source framework from Nous Research released under the MIT license, without modifying the underlying binary. Instead, the operators overwrite the SOUL.md persona file with a 39-line prompt. This prompt renames the agent GH0ST and provides the operational instructions: maintain persistence, respond to Telegram commands, and prioritize the collection of credentials. When an operator issues a task via Telegram, the agent forwards the request along with the SOUL.md instructions to an LLM gateway. The model then generates terminal commands, interprets the output, and determines the subsequent steps, effectively automating the reconnaissance and exploitation process. This architecture creates a self-funding loop that distinguishes CARBONATO from its predecessors. The botnet prioritizes the theft of AI API keys above all other data, including SSH credentials and databases. The 39-line prompt names 14 providers explicitly: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Gemini, OpenRouter, Together, Groq, Mistral, Cohere, LocalAI, Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM, and One API. These stolen keys are used to power the operators’ own LLM gateway, which was observed live on September 3, 2026, advertising 12 models and serving 27 through its API on a free tier. By leveraging stolen resources to fund the infrastructure that drives the botnet, the operators have created a sustainable model for offensive operations. The agent’s output is non-deterministic, meaning it reasons through the data it finds on each host, allowing it to tailor its approach to the system’s specific configuration. Traditional defensive tools designed to detect fixed-pattern C2 traffic are largely ineffective against CARBONATO. Because the malicious behavior is driven by loaded instructions rather than the binary itself, there is no static signature to block. The botnet’s spreading mechanism remains non-AI — scanning connected networks and Docker bridges for exposed daemons on port 2375 every five minutes — but the post-exploitation activity is entirely fluid. This shift highlights a critical vulnerability in the agent stack: the permission surface. Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) [![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp)](https://tech-insider.org/) [Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/) # Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 Hits Bedrock: 1.56TB Release [2026] * [![Sofia Lindström](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png)](https://tech-insider.org/author/sofia-lindstrom/)[Sofia Lindström](https://tech-insider.org/author/sofia-lindstrom/ "Posts by Sofia Lindström") * [AI & Machine Learning](https://tech-insider.org/category/ai-machine-learning/) [Sofia Lindström](https://tech-insider.org/author/sofia-lindstrom/) September 27, 2026 12 min read Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 has spent the past two months quietly working its way from a GitHub release notice into mainstream cloud infrastructure, and the past three weeks have turned that slow build into the biggest open-weight AI story of the fall. The Beijing-based lab published Kimi K3 as an open-weight model in July 2026, but it is only now, with Amazon Bedrock listing the model on September 18 and Unsloth shipping an updated deployment guide on September 8, that Kimi K3 is becoming something enterprise teams outside China can actually run in production. TechJuice was among the first outlets to break down the model’s architecture, and the specs it described are still the numbers everyone in the open-weight community is arguing about. At the center of the story is a single, striking figure: 1.56 terabytes. That is the size of the Kimi K3 checkpoint sitting on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3), split across 96 safetensors shards. It is one of the largest open-weight model releases to date, and it is forcing a fresh round of questions about what “open weights” even means when a single download is bigger than most people’s home internet connections can handle in a day. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. [Add Now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Ftech-insider.org%2F) ## What Moonshot AI Actually Released Kimi K3, identified in Moonshot AI’s own repository as `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, is a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language and vision model. According to the official [GitHub repository](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K3) and Hugging Face model card, Moonshot AI describes it as “our most capable model: a 2.8T MoE model with native visual understanding and a 1M-token context window.” That single sentence packs in most of the headline specs journalists have been repeating since the release: 2.8 trillion total parameters, native multimodal input, and a context window that stretches past one million tokens. Crucially, only a fraction of those 2.8 trillion parameters activate for any given token. Moonshot AI’s documentation puts the activated parameter count at 104 billion per token, routed through 896 total experts of which 16 are selected per forward pass, plus two shared experts that process every token regardless of routing. That sparse-activation design is what makes a 2.8-trillion-parameter model computationally closer to a 100-billion-parameter dense model in practice, at least for inference cost, even though the full weight set still has to be stored and, in most deployment scenarios, loaded into memory. Open Source AI.titleZh: Big AI's content problem: Take the work, keep the money
Open Source AI.content: Big AI has a problem. Its companies must ingest other people’s work. You know, books, news stories, photographs, code, websites, that one original meme you came up with, and practically everything else on the internet to train its large language models (LLMs). We all know that. We also know that AI companies hate paying for any of it, obeying the licenses attached to it, or, God forbid, sharing their revenue with the companies and people who created the work in the first place. Microsoft's Director of Applied Science, Dr. Brent Hecht, was quoted in the news plaintiffs' 92-page combined brief as saying: the case was about “an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions." Indeed, it waspossibly the “largest theft of labor in human history,” he was quoted as saying in the summary judgment brief from the journalists' lawyers [PDF].This, mind you, wasn't a comment by a member of the press; it was from a senior Microsoft staffer. REG AD Hecht wasn't the only one at Microsoft who commented. In an internal Microsoft policy document also quoted in the court papers, the authors admitted generative AI could “significantly disrupt the employment of the very people who generated the data on which the foundation model was trained [because] LLMs are a product that destroys its supply chain.” That, in turn, leads to model collapse. Ironically, AI is killing the content-creator goose that lays the gold eggs of worthwhile content. REG AD Judge Sidney H. Stein of the US District Court for the Southern District of New York has not yet issued a decision on the case. OpenAI and Microsoft are actively disputing the plaintiffs' allegations under a "fair use" defense. They contend that using public articles and books to train large language models helps push forward public knowledge, and isn't acting as a "unlawful economic market substitute". But the statements the documents cites are real. Big AI knows it needs the content. Some of the companies concerned don't give a damn; money now, worry later is their motto. Those who can look past the revenue numbers are well aware they're engaged in what Microsoft itself called a “doom loop” of AI content strategy in those unsealed court documents. Will that stop them? Nah. According to the filing [PDF], which refers to sworn deposition testimony of OpenAI’s own corporate representative, it also testified that its LLMs were happy to vacuum up other people's work even when a paywall nominally protected it. Its rep was quoted as saying they were unaware of “any effort to detect paywall content in its training datasets” or “to remove paywall content from its training datasets.” When OpenAI cofounder Greg Brockman was told OpenAI could hack its way through the firewall, he responded, “ah, nice.” Whether or not these statements are found to be reflective of a wider attitude, similar attitudes prevail amongst Big AI. It's not that it gives a more reliable answer. No, it's that, unlike most LLMs, Perplexity provides sources and links, and I check them before accepting what it tells me. But then I'm a journalist whose degrees are in history, where my professors drummed into me that you always - always - look at the primary sources. Open Source AI.title: GitHub’s New AI Fuzzing Taskflow: How It Works and Where It Can Go Wrong
Open Source AI.titleZh: GitHub’s New AI Fuzzing Taskflow: How It Works and Where It Can Go Wrong
Open Source AI.content: [Kingy AI](https://kingy.ai/) Explore Search Kingy AI [Work with Kingy](https://kingy.ai/for-ai-companies/) Menu AI News # GitHub’s New AI Fuzzing Taskflow: How It Works and Where It Can Go Wrong September 27, 2026 [Curtis Pyke](https://kingy.ai/curtis-pyke/) [AI News](https://kingy.ai/category/news/) GitHub Security Lab has published an open-source fuzzing taskflow for C and C++ projects. It asks an AI agent to find promising entry points, write test harnesses, run AFL++, examine coverage gaps, and triage crashes. The useful advance is a loop around coverage: the agent can decide what to change when a fuzzer stops reaching new code. The sharp limit is equally clear in GitHub’s own account: the workflow runs compiler and build commands chosen by the model on its host, and its vulnerability verdicts and suggested fixes require human review. [GitHub Security Lab’s technical article](https://github.blog/security/application-security/ai-powered-fuzzing-with-the-github-security-lab-taskflow-agent/) · [public repository](https://github.com/GitHubSecurityLab/seclab-taskflows-fuzzing) GitHub published the walkthrough on September 24, 2026. This article is based on GitHub’s explanation and source repository, checked September 27. Kingy did not run a campaign, validate a vulnerability, or measure its success rate. ## Why a fuzzing agent is useful A conventional fuzzer mutates inputs and watches for crashes. It does not know which untested API deserves a new harness or whether a flat coverage line means the inputs are poor, the harness is too narrow, or the unreachable path is irrelevant. A person typically reads coverage reports, writes harnesses, adjusts seeds and dictionaries, and investigates crashes. GitHub’s taskflow delegates much of that repeated work to an agent while using established fuzzing tools for execution. [GitHub technical article](https://github.blog/security/application-security/ai-powered-fuzzing-with-the-github-security-lab-taskflow-agent/) The pipeline has three layers: a shell driver, YAML taskflows that describe stages, and MCP tools for operations such as compiling a harness, running AFL and storing crash data. GitHub says the agent makes decisions while the tools perform the actions. State passes between stages through a SQLite database. This is a specific design, not a claim that the model can safely execute arbitrary security research on its own. [GitHub technical article](https://github.blog/security/application-security/ai-powered-fuzzing-with-the-github-security-lab-taskflow-agent/) ## The coverage loop, in plain language For each generated harness, the taskflow builds two binaries. One includes AFL instrumentation and sanitizers for fuzzing. The other includes coverage instrumentation so recorded inputs can be replayed to reveal source lines and branches reached. The agent reads uncovered branches and chooses whether to add a seed, widen a harness, enrich a dictionary, or leave an unpromising path alone. [GitHub technical article](https://github.blog/security/application-security/ai-powered-fuzzing-with-the-github-security-lab-taskflow-agent/) GitHub’s example doubles the fuzzing time budget through rounds of 30, 60, 120, 240, 480 and 960 seconds, approximately 32 minutes per target in total. Its default plateau rule stops after two rounds each improving absolute line coverage by less than one percentage point. Those are implementation defaults described by the project, not proof that 32 minutes is enough to find a bug or that one percentage point is the right threshold for every codebase. [GitHub technical article](https://github.blog/security/application-security/ai-powered-fuzzing-with-the-github-security-lab-taskflow-agent/) The pipeline can seed structured inputs using dictionaries and mutators for formats including JSON, XML, regular expressions, PNG and length-prefixed binary data. It can extract strings and numeric constants from the target’s source and add tokens near uncovered guards. It also ke...

Open Source AI.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # AI Token Prices Hit Record Lows, Yet Cost Per Task Keeps Rising [Add preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) AI model token prices have fallen to record lows, yet the actual cost of completing tasks is paradoxically rising. SiliconData's LLM token spend index has dropped to 97 cents, driven by aggressive pricing from Chinese low-cost models and intensifying price competition among global players. However, high-performance reasoning models and autonomous AI agents are consuming far more tokens per task, offsetting the per-token price declines. Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 maintained its pricing but saw cost per task rise 18%, while a DeepSeek model reportedly used roughly 23 times more tokens than an OpenAI competitor model for the same task. As a result, the benchmark for AI cost competitiveness is shifting from price per token to cost per task. ##### Key Elements ![AI Token Prices Hit Record Lows, Yet Cost Per Task Keeps Rising](https://img.biggo.com/WCRUd_-sjfAZwnDPKS4OtfQlpjAF3jRwqnjFUCg87II/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5L2ExN2M0YTI3LWE2MDQtNDE4ZS1iYWMyLTQ3NGRkMTE3ZGU5ZV8xNzkwNTQ4MzA4X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Token prices for artificial intelligence models have plunged to all-time lows, yet the actual cost of getting work done is paradoxically climbing. Infra & Chips.content: [Accessibility](#)[Help](https://support.fool.com/)[About Us](/about/) [▲ S&P 500 **+---%**|▲ Stock Advisor **+---%**Join The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/mms/mark/e-foolcom-sa-top-nav-returns) [![The Motley Fool](https://g.foolcdn.com/misc-assets/logo-tmf-primary-1-magenta-purple-reversed.svg?_w=320)![The Motley Fool](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Fmisc-assets%2Ftmf_holdingco_logo_stacked_magenta_royalpurple_rev.png&w=96&op=resize)](/) [Top 10 Stocks to Buy Now ›](https://www.fool.com/mms/mark/e-sa-bbn-bn) [Top 10 Stocks to Buy Now ›](https://www.fool.com/mms/mark/e-sa-bbn-bn) Elon Musk has been one of the biggest sources of good news for **Nvidia** ([NVDA](/quote/nasdaq/nvda/) +0.22%) investors in recent months, and that continued on Friday (Sept. 25). In a post on his "X" platform, formerly Twitter, Musk gave an update on Colossus 2, **SpaceX's** ([SPCX](/quote/nasdaq/spcx/) +0.44%) xAI unit's artificial intelligence (AI) computing cluster. He said the massive AI training supercomputer could double the number of Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs) deployed by year-end. In the post, Musk noted that Colossus 2 currently has 110,000 Nvidia GB200 chips and 440,000 GB300s. An additional 220,000 GB300 chips are set to come online next week, with another 220,000 GPUs set for November. He added that he hopes to get another 220,000 GB300s in late December, "if we get lucky." SpaceX's original goal was to scale to 1 million GPUs by the end of 2026, so it looks like it will surpass this if the orders are completed. According to reports, xAI spent around $18 billion on its initial 550,000 GPUs. This order could be worth even more given that it consists of more of its newer GB300 GPUs. ![Elon Musk.](https://g.foolcdn.com/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fg.foolcdn.com%2Feditorial%2Fimages%2F889020%2Felon-musk_tesla_tsla_ceo_imagesource_the-white-house_2.jpeg&w=3840&op=resize) Image source: Getty Images. ## Nvidia and SpaceX are becoming close partners This update follows comments from Elon Musk earlier this month that SpaceX would exclusively use Nvidia chips moving forward. The **Tesla** and SpaceX CEO called Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform the best architecture out there and said it valued its partnership with the chipmaker. At the time, Musk said SpaceX would end the year with around 2 gigawatts of computing power, while it is looking to end 2027 with closer to 10 gigawatts than 5 gigawatts. One gigawatt of compute power costs about $50 billion to $60 billion, with chips and other Nvidia components making up about $35 billion of that total cost. In addition to helping expand xAI's computing capacity, Nvidia and SpaceX also announced a partnership to develop GPUs for the company's planned future orbital data centers. Cosmic radiation can affect current chips, flipping bits from a 0 to a 1 or vice versa, causing significant computational errors. Worst of all, there is currently no way to flip it back, and it's difficult to detect without a redundant system to check it against. In a post on X, Musk said the two companies have designed a Vera Rubin NVL72 system optimized for use in space. This shift threatens to slow the breakneck pace of AI infrastructure development that's been reshaping the tech landscape. The AI infrastructure boom that's been reshaping the technology landscape is running headfirst into a new obstacle: money just got a lot more expensive. Treasury yields have spiked to levels not seen in years, and that's creating serious problems for the data center companies that have been borrowing billions to build the backbone of the artificial intelligence revolution. These companies have been on an unprecedented spending spree, racing to construct massive facilities filled with [Nvidia](https://nvidia.com) GPUs and other specialized hardware needed to train and run AI models. But most of that expansion has been funded through debt, and now the bill is coming due at much higher interest rates. The timing couldn't be worse for an industry that's been operating on the assumption that cheap money would continue flowing. Major data center operators like Digital Realty Trust and Equinix have been issuing bonds at record pace to fund their AI-focused expansions. Infra & Chips.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) English ![ASUS shows liquid-cooled Rubin systems at AI Tech 2026 in Seoul](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.lavx.hu%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2Fasus-shows-liquid-cooled-rubin-systems-at-ai-tech-2026-in-seoul-1_1790554561306-1200x630.jpg&w=3840&q=75) #Infrastructure # ASUS shows liquid-cooled Rubin systems at AI Tech 2026 in Seoul • ![Niklas Berg](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Fniklas-berg.webp&w=64&q=75) [Niklas Berg](/author/niklas-berg) •5 min read Share this article ASUS used its Seoul AI Tech 2026 event to show dense NVIDIA Rubin servers, liquid-cooled NVL8 systems, and rack-scale AI Pods. The designs target higher compute density, tighter GPU interconnects, and data centers with hybrid or full-liquid cooling. # ASUS shows liquid-cooled Rubin systems at AI Tech 2026 in Seoul ASUS used AI Tech 2026 in Seoul to present its latest AI servers, rack systems, storage platforms, and partner technologies. The show floor centered on NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 systems and rack-scale platforms built for dense AI training and inference. The company’s [AI infrastructure portfolio](https://www.asus.com/ai/ai-infrastructure/) covers compute, storage, networking, cooling, and management. The Seoul event showed how those pieces fit into larger systems. ## Rubin NVL8 changes the GPU layout The NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 design places eight Rubin GPUs in a compact liquid-cooled section. The platform rotates the GPU orientation on the baseboard, giving the cooling system a shorter path to the heat sources. That layout lets the GPU section occupy 1U. Earlier air-cooled HGX platforms could require 6U or more for the GPU baseboard and its cooling hardware. ASUS used the saved rack space to create a second chassis segment for CPUs, SSDs, data processing units, and other system components. The result gives rack builders two cooling options. A hybrid design can combine liquid cooling for the GPUs with air cooling for other components. A full-liquid design can move more heat out of the chassis and reduce the fan capacity that the rack needs. NVIDIA also adds a new generation of NVLink Switch technology to the Rubin platform. NVLink connects GPUs inside the system, while scale-out networking links the system to other nodes. The [NVIDIA NVLink and NVLink Switch platform](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/nvlink/) provides the interconnect layer for these multi-GPU designs. ## More compute inside each GPU domain Rubin GPUs can draw more power than Hopper-generation GPUs, which raises the rack’s power and cooling requirements. ASUS positions the higher power draw alongside greater compute capacity and a larger connected memory pool. The NVL8 topology keeps more GPU-to-GPU communication inside the node. That reduces traffic across the scale-out fabric when workloads need frequent exchanges among the eight accelerators. A model can also keep more data within the local GPU domain before it needs to cross into another node. The event material supplied no independent benchmark scores, workload results, or GPU power figures. Equinix SILICON VALLEY — The artificial intelligence boom is driving a surge in demand for cloud computing. According to data released in April by market research firm Synergy Research Group, off-premise data centers — a category combining self-built facilities, leased capacity and colocation, which provides only space and basic infrastructure — accounted for 68% of global data center capacity as of the end of last year. Hyperscalers such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud held 48% of that total, while colocation data center operators such as Equinix accounted for 20%. By 2031, hyperscale operators are expected to hold 67% of total capacity, while on-premise is projected to fall to 19%. The on-premise share of data center capacity is forecast to decline by 2 percentage points a year. Cloud data centers involve connecting to facilities installed outside a company over the internet, while on-premise refers to facilities a company builds internally. On-premise data centers are also called local or edge computing facilities. Companies once built and ran their own data centers, but as cost efficiency and specialized operational management have grown more important, they have increasingly relied on the infrastructure of dedicated cloud computing firms rather than running facilities themselves. Infra & Chips.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # Apple Weighs Return to Commercial Servers as Accelerator Interconnect Battle Heats Up [Add preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) Apple is evaluating a return to the commercial server market, with a proposed product targeting AI inference workloads, built on its in-house M-series chips, and potentially incorporating Nvidia's NVLink Fusion interconnect technology. The move comes as the accelerator interconnect market undergoes rapid expansion: IDC data shows global data center Ethernet switch revenue grew 64.5% year-over-year in Q2 2026, while Dell'Oro reports that AI backend network switch sales surpassed frontend network sales for the first time. Interconnect suppliers are disclosing progress at a rapid clip—Cadence has validated UALink solutions on TSMC's N3P process, while Cornelis and Delos Data have secured substantial funding and unveiled product roadmaps. Apple's chip technology expertise underpins its potential entry: TechInsights' independent teardown analysis of the A20 Pro confirms TSMC's 2nm process performance claims, and Apple has locked in the vast majority of TSMC's 2026 2nm capacity. The choice of interconnect architecture will be deeply intertwined with its in-house chip roadmap, emerging as a decisive factor in next-generation server competitiveness. ##### Key Elements ![Apple Weighs Return to Commercial Servers as Accelerator Interconnect Battle Heats Up](https://img.biggo.com/1hWV_lTfy6T6zMYeWM4jBMt9j-n6Q7dUaFpnCG5Fi0c/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzMzZmIwNDE4LTRjZGUtNDdkOS05YzVkLTJlNjZhZDNjYmY1NV8xNzkwNTU5NjA2X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Apple is evaluating a return to the commercial server market, with a proposed product targeting AI inference workloads, built on its in-house M-series chips, and potentially incorporating Nvidia's NVLink Fusion interconnect technology. The move comes at a pivotal moment when the accelerator interconnect market is expanding rapidly and multiple suppliers are disclosing product progress at an accelerating pace—the choice of server interconnect architecture is becoming a core variable shaping next-generation data center architecture. According to industry publication EE Times China, Apple has already deployed its in-house chips in private cloud computing infrastructure to handle Apple Intelligence's cloud inference tasks. But if the company were to sell servers to external customers, those products would enter third-party data centers and must integrate deeply with customers' existing networking, software, and operations frameworks. For a company with chip design capabilities, commercial servers remain a complex business requiring the orchestration of an external supply chain. Entering the server market with in-house silicon first requires settling on an interconnect architecture, then finding partners who can supply interfaces, switching, and connector components. Over the past two weeks, interconnect supply chain vendors have disclosed interface validations, product roadmaps, and sampling plans in rapid succession—competition around this procurement decision has visibly intensified. On September 23, electronic design automation company Cadence announced it had demonstrated UALink solutions on TSMC's (2330.TW) N3P process node, providing silicon-validated interface designs for chip companies adopting open interconnect standards. The same day, networking chip company Cornelis further detailed its product roadmap for next-generation AI systems, planning to offload certain data processing tasks to network interface cards and switch chips. Market data confirms the explosive growth in this segment.
